findings.claim: The retirement sends all hands-on SQL and JDBC assessment to the graded practical, which is not in this tree, and the record does not track that as an open item. The blueprint instructions (blueprint.json line 258) tell learners that writing SQL and JDBC 'is assessed separately, in the course's graded practical'. md lines 16, 42 and 72 name it sql-jdbc-graded-practical with a 120-minute, 180-minute-pair design. But course.json assessments lists only sql-module-check, and the practical exists only at 4cbf022b on the unlanded fm/pep-laa-sql-jdbc branch. md line 72 says 'to be re-read after it lands', yet Open items 1 to 4 have no entry for it. That practical's own instructions still say the sql-module-check coding part 'is unchanged by this branch', which contradicts the retirement. If this branch lands first, the course's graded assessment set briefly has no hands-on component, and a learner-facing instruction points at an assessment learners cannot see. Also, two taught objectives are now assessed by neither the MCQ nor the practical: group-by-and-having#o3 and seeding-sample-data#o2 (create-table#o1 is in the practical).
findings.recommendation: Add Open item 5, 'Graded practical landing', with the closure steps in the sql-intake-edu-003 recheck: land the practical, list it in course.json assessments, fix its 'Relation to sql-module-check' sentence, and re-read its objective list. Sequence the landings so the practical lands with or before this retirement, or record a captain-accepted gap window. Note group-by#o3 and seeding#o2 as assessed by neither graded instrument, so the reconciler can accept or reassign them.

findings.claim: The item-26 note added under Open item 4 for final-sme-103 described the private item's code structure in a way that, read with the public plannedContext in the coverage map, lets a reader without the private bank infer the keyed outcome. That is the same class of leak as final-edu-003 and final-edu-201, now in the committed record rather than the map, and it contradicts the record's own rule against stating keyed responses (md lines 5 and 102).
findings.recommendation: Reduce the note to a value-free validity statement that does not describe the item's code or outcome. For example: 'Item 26 (finding final-sme-103): a private check confirmed that the SQLite run and PostgreSQL semantics agree for this item; it stays in the PostgreSQL run.' Keep the reasoning in private staging.

findings.claim: Applying the item-14 containment standard consistently, line 215 (item 16 plannedContext) and line 294 (item 22 stepUp) named the item's triggering condition rather than only its symptom or added difficulty, and line 380 (item 29 plannedContext) was borderline. No option, key or value is stated, so it is low.
findings.recommendation: Reword those lines in symptom-only or difficulty-only form. No private item change is needed.
